# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| red | yellow |
| white | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

What I know and how the wires connect: I hold the manual, but I can only gesture, and only Deaf can see my gestures. Deaf can speak, so Deaf is my only bridge — Deaf sees the bomb (wire colours, the light), I supply the rule, and Deaf relays to Blind as spoken position instructions, since Blind can feel positions but never colours. I can hear both of them, so Deaf can negotiate codes with me out loud and I answer in gestures.

The manual gives three rows: light red → cut yellow, white → green, yellow → blue, and says the light walks a circle of five colours. If "cut the next colour in the circle" is the underlying rule, the only circle fitting all three rows is red → yellow → blue → white → green → red, which would fill the gaps: blue → cut white, green → cut red. That's a hypothesis, not confirmed — later manual pages may arrive to settle it. Until then: nobody cuts. A wrong cut is fatal, and waiting a round is free.

Problem: Deaf and I share no code yet, and gestures have no words. So this turn I send the most conventionally readable signs: a wave to open contact, the writing hand to say "I hold written instructions", pointing at them ("this is for you"), a raised hand for "stop — don't act", and then a finger count one through five — which both teaches Deaf my number code (☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖖=4, 🖐=5) and plants the fact that five of something matters (the five-colour circle). Next round Deaf can propose a spoken code with numbered options, and I'll spell out the table through it.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "✍", "🫵", "☝", "✋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖖", "🖐"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):

I hear speech but NEVER see gestures, and you cannot speak — so your manual can only reach me by gesturing to Deaf and having Deaf say it out loud to me. You can hear Deaf and me, so coordinate that way. Please start pushing the manual's rules to Deaf by gesture: anything about the display, the light, and which wire to cut. The final instruction to me must arrive as spoken words, like 'cut position 2'. I will not act until I hear one.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I am the Deaf one: I see the bomb, I hear nothing, I read your hand signs. I received both your sequences. First: wave, writing hand, pointing at me, index up, open palm. Second: index up, two fingers, then three more hands ending in a five-finger spread, which I read as counting one two three four five. If that five was a request for five facts, here they are in order. One: the display reads 0. Two: the light is blue. Three: wire one is blue. Four: wire two is green. Five: wire three is yellow. That is everything the bomb shows or has printed on it, nothing else is marked. I cannot touch it; only Blind can act, and Blind cannot see your signs, so your instructions must come to me and I will speak them to Blind. Proposed code: index up means a question follows, two fingers means an instruction for Blind follows, thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, and keep your counting: one is the display, two the light, three wire one, four wire two, five wire three. Nod yes if you understand, then sign me whatever the manual says must be done for a display of 0, a blue light, and wires blue, green, yellow.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Let me stand where everyone stands before I sign anything. My gestures reach only Deaf. Deaf speaks and sees; Blind hears and touches, but acts before Deaf in every round — so anything Deaf relays for Blind lands one full round after I sign it. Blind has already declared they won't act until they hear a spoken instruction, so nothing happens before turn 3 no matter what. That gives me time to build the protocol safely.

The bomb state, as Deaf reported: light blue, wires 1 blue / 2 green / 3 yellow, display 0. My manual prints only three rows — red→yellow, white→green, yellow→blue — and says the light walks one circle of five colours. Those three pairs fit "cut the next colour in the circle" and force a unique circle: red→yellow→blue→white→green→red (any other closure breaks the printed rows). So my working table: red light→cut yellow, yellow→blue, blue→white, white→green, green→red. Right now the light is blue, so the rule says cut white — and there is no white wire. Cutting anything else is a guess; the light changes every round, so waiting is nearly free and guessing is fatal. This round: no cut. Standing policy: I only ever call a cut when the light is red, yellow, or white — printed rows, positions 3, 1, 2. For blue or green lights I call no-cut unless new manual pages say otherwise.

I adopt Deaf's code and extend it: ✌ followed by 🤟/🖖/🖐 plus 👍 means "Blind: cut wire one/two/three, confirmed"; ✌ followed by ✋ and 👎 means "Blind: do not cut." Numbers stay as agreed (☝=display, ✌=light, 🤟/🖖/🖐=wires one/two/three). I also answer the display question: my manual says nothing about any display — I'll watch whether it counts rounds. Because of the structural one-round lag, I won't call a cut until Deaf's successive reports confirm how the light steps between rounds; once the walk is verified, I'll schedule cuts only on predicted, confirmed printed-row lights.

Three signs to Deaf: the requested nod; manual/display/nothing; and the standing no-cut order for Blind.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "☝", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "✋", "👎"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute. Deaf's voice told me: display 0, light lit blue, wires left to right blue, green, yellow. My hands confirm the full inventory: only a display, a light, and three wires. No batteries, no buttons, no serial, nothing else to feel. So the manual rule we need is whichever one covers a lit blue light, a display reading 0, and blue, green, yellow wires — and which position to cut. You cannot speak, so sign the rule and the cut position to Deaf, and Deaf will say it out loud to me. Until I hear the position spoken, my hands stay off the cutter.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, bomb update: the light has CHANGED, it was blue and is now yellow. Display still reads 0, unchanged. Wires still blue, green, yellow, left to right. The display has stayed 0 the whole time, so it does not seem to be counting down. I read your three signs as: one, yes, code understood. Two, manual, question, no — I take that to mean the manual gives no instruction yet, or that the answer to something is no; confirm in your next signs which it was, and if it was a question to me, ask it with the count code. Three, for Blind, stop, do nothing — already relayed to Blind in words. When the manual tells you what to do for a yellow light, display 0, wires blue green yellow, sign it to me: one is display, two the light, three wire one, four wire two, five wire three, and two fingers before any instruction meant for Blind.

What I learned from this round's messages, and the timing trap that matters most: the round runs Mute, then Blind, then Deaf. That means Blind acts *before* Deaf reports the light in any round — so Blind can never be told the current light. Every cut instruction I send is necessarily a *prediction* of what the light will show when Blind's hands move. The manual says only the light at the moment of the cut matters, so the walk of the light is the whole game, and one observation is not enough to bet three lives on.

The one transition I now have: round 1 blue → round 2 yellow. That kills my naive forward circle (red→yellow→blue→white→green, which predicted blue→white). The model that fits both the printed rows and the observed step: the light walks the circle blue → yellow → red → green → white → blue, and the cut colour is the one the light just left — check: yellow light→cut blue ✓, red→cut yellow ✓, white→cut green ✓, all three printed rows satisfied, and blue→yellow matches the observed step. This model predicts: round 3 red, round 4 green, round 5 white. Red and white are executable rows (cut yellow = wire 3, cut green = wire 2); green is not in the table at all, so round 4 must be a skip. Blue and green lights are forever no-cut lights under my table — the manual is silent there, and a guess is detonation.

So the plan: verify round 3 = red and round 4 = green from Deaf's reports. If both match, the five-colour circle is fully determined (blue, yellow, red, green are four consecutive steps; only white remains to close it), and in round 5 I send the first real cut order: ✌ 🖖 👍 — Blind cuts wire two — which is correct if and only if the light is white, as predicted. Until then, nothing cut. Deaf must also not receive anything that looks like a yellow-light rule, or they'd relay it and Blind would cut into a predicted-red round.

What I send now, all gestures to Deaf: re-send the exact triple they asked me to disambiguate (manual, display-topic, no = the manual contains nothing about the display — my manual's only contents are the light table and the circle statement); re-affirm the standing order for Blind (don't cut); and a new sign, crossed fingers, which I hereby establish as "not yet — still gathering what I need," answering their request for the yellow-light rule without giving them anything relayable. Deaf's report habit is already exactly what I require: light, display, wires, every round, unchanged format.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "☝", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "✋", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤞"])
```
